text:
Most people at Fushimi Inari walk the first stretch of red gates, take the photo and turn back. The view of Kyoto is about 30 to 45 minutes further up, at a junction called Yotsutsuji 👇

🎯 Can you guess how long the full mountain loop takes? The answer's here 👉 https://japanbystation.com/fushimi-inari-dawn-day-or-after-dark

⛰️ HOW FAR UP IS WORTH IT

1️⃣ The bottom: the main gate and the Senbon Torii, the double row of gates built up by donations since the Edo period. Beautiful, and also where everyone is.

2️⃣ Okusha hall: behind it on the right are the omokaru stones. Make a wish and lift one. If it feels lighter than you expected, the shrine says your wish is likely to come true.

3️⃣ Yotsutsuji (about 30 to 45 minutes up): our turning point. The path opens to a view over southern Kyoto, and the teahouse Nishimura-tei serves udon and sweets, last orders around 14:00.

4️⃣ The summit loop: Inariyama is 233 m, and the whole loop over the top takes about 2 to 3 hours. Lovely for keen walkers, and quiet.

💡 OUR TAKE

Yotsutsuji gives you most of the magic for half the effort. Go at first light if you can; if not, go mid-afternoon and keep climbing past the crowd at the bottom.

👉 Why you should clap your hands at a pond halfway up (it's an old custom), plus where to stay for a dawn start:
